title: PIN-bearing user-management recovery DTOs retained as plaintext local JSON
confidence: HIGH for serialization path; actual credential access/exposure UNKNOWN
source: Legitimate operator InitialPin or CurrentPin/NewPin held by public typed request records
sink: File.WriteAllText of serialized envelope Payload=request, then File.Move to per-station local profile journal
boundary: Trusted secret-entry UI/API request becomes plaintext persisted filesystem data readable to principals with Windows profile/file access; no remote unauthenticated boundary demonstrated

evidence.evidence: Actual app initializes FileRetainedRequestStore for cashier before VM creation.
Public positional InitialPin property, no JsonIgnore or masking converter.
Public CurrentPin/NewPin properties; CurrentPin null only admin path.
Durable fixed owner keys users.create and users.change-pin.
CreateUserRequest captures InitialPin and passes to durable _pendingCreate.SendAsync.
ChangePinRequest captures current/new PIN and passes durable _pendingPin.SendAsync; visible field clearing on success does not itself guarantee filesystem removal.
First pending request saved before send; success/non-null or definite initial failure clears via store; unresolved record retained.
Serializer options only WriteIndented=false; no credential converter/encryption. Directory created without explicit custom ACL.
Path derived from Windows LocalApplicationData/Falah/pending-operations/station plus safe owner key.
Envelope includes original typed object as Payload; JSON written to .tmp in plaintext, moved to .json; errors callback optional and do not prevent network operation.
Clear attempts deleting primary .json only; failures swallowed through callback, no .tmp cleanup.

preconditions: Legitimate account creation or PIN change is attempted with actual file store active and writable.
Local principal or another permitted collection mechanism can read that profile file/temp/copy while bytes persist.
No claim a lower-privilege Windows account bypasses profile ACLs.
counterevidence: Per-user Windows LocalApplicationData commonly inherits profile access controls; deployed ACLs not inspected and no weakness asserted.
Known successful and first definite rejected outcomes normally attempt deletion, limiting primary-file lifetime.
Unwritable save can produce no primary file; existence on any real station not established.
Stored server PIN hashes are a separate control: this finding concerns client plaintext request retention only.
Station separation avoids inter-client collision, but does not encrypt credentials.

additional_source_observation.description: If writing .tmp succeeds and subsequent move fails, catch does not remove .tmp; later Clear deletes only .json. Thus main-record clearing is not proof every temporary secret copy was removed. No actual temp file examined or created.

rubric_results.criterion: Actual production App initializes file store before user VM request restoration.
PIN-bearing typed requests flow through durable owner-key helper before transport.
Actual serializer/file sink retains public PIN properties without encryption/redaction.
Lifecycle/ACL/local-access counterevidence and temp-file failures constrain exposure.
Disposition separates source-confirmed retention from unverified real files/access/exfiltration.

tested: Actual code, public DTO properties, serializer options, caller ordering and clear/failure branches inspected; source/hash/span/symbol identities checked. No runtime serializer, file-store instance, user login, network request or database test executed.
proof_gaps: No real pending record, PIN, ACL, process token, backup copy or live filesystem permissions collected.
No exploit or account takeover demonstrated.
Local secret-retention policy and Windows user sharing/deployment remain unknown.
recommended_remediation: Prefer credential-free durable recovery/status keyed by server-owned operation identity. If credentials must briefly persist, approved OS-protected per-user storage and explicit cleanup/failure lifecycle are required; preserve ambiguous-outcome reconciliation.
regression_risks: Removing secret-bearing recovery fields without protocol change can strand uncertain account creation/PIN changes or repeat credential writes.
required_tests: Fake store/serializer tests assert no real or synthetic PIN values in durable representation.
Known success/rejection/ambiguous/recovered flows retain recovery correctness without secret persistence.
Controlled fake filesystem write-success/move-failure proves temp cleanup without operating on real journals.
minimal_next_step: Design testable credential-free recovery contract and, under separate explicit authorization, validate isolated storage serialization/cleanup using synthetic secrets only.
